concept: Menu is a key that opens the same plastic panel as Select, holding a few actions printed in ink as words with a glyph; the one that removes something carries the critical lamp shape beside its word, never a colour.

default_to_avoid.pattern: Radix or MUI dropdown menu with a blue highlighted row and keyboard shortcut hints
default_to_avoid.why_not: A tinted bar for the focused row tells position by colour alone, and shortcut hints print a second column of text a phone user can never press.

default_to_avoid.pattern: destructive menu item painted red or orange
default_to_avoid.why_not: A red or orange word tells the danger by colour alone, and orange is kept for the one primary control of a unit under P1.

references.source: Braun SK 4 radio-phonograph (Dieter Rams, Hans Gugelot, 1956): functions printed in plain words beside each part, one column, no colour coding
Braun T 1000 world receiver (Dieter Rams, 1963): a lid that opens over the controls to show a printed panel of functions
WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices: menu button pattern (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menu-button/)

derivation.form: The open panel is surface.solid plastic with elevation.float and corner.inner on layer.overlay, the same panel Select opens and nothing deeper.

derivation.consequence: links, borders, icons, selections and charts never use it
derivation.form: Every action is primary ink; the focused row is a recess and a destructive action is a square critical lamp beside its word, never orange.

derivation.consequence: every part keeps ≥44px hit area even when it draws smaller
derivation.form: The trigger is a 44px round key and every action row is at least control.md tall, as wide as the longest word.

derivation.consequence: every mechanism has its keyboard map
derivation.form: Enter, Space and Down open on the first action, Up on the last, arrows, Home, End and letters move, Escape closes and returns focus to the key.

derivation.consequence: no entry choreography, no idle animation; transitions only on state
derivation.form: The panel rises off the key when it opens and sinks back toward it faster when it closes (D-008), and it flips above the key when there is no room below.

options.name: plastic panel under the key, rows as printing, focused row a recess, destructive action last after a gap
a bank of round keys beside the trigger, each word printed under its key
no popup: the row opens in place into a card of actions with seams

variants.reason: A reuses Select's panel so a person learns one popup, grows to its longest action and holds five actions as easily as three (P3 44px rows); B runs out of width at four actions and stacks long words, and C pushes the rows below down when it opens, against P6 fixed positions so a unit's layout does not reflow between states.

root.why: The menu takes only the space of its key in the row, so it sits on the row's inset line like any other part.

chevron.why: A word key that opens a menu prints a small chevron after its word, flat ink with no shadow and no emboss.

panel.why: The open menu is a plastic panel with one short soft shadow on the overlay layer, the same panel as Select's list.

item.why: Each action row is at least 44px tall with its words inset from the rounded ends, so a finger can press it.

icon.why: An action's glyph is printed in secondary ink at the start of the row, above 3:1 on the panel plastic.

lamp.why: A destructive action carries the critical lamp, a filled square, so the danger is a shape beside a word and never orange.

text.why: Action words use the body size of the one grotesk and stay on one line while the panel grows to the longest word.

destructive.why: A destructive action sits after a gap at the end of the panel, apart from the actions that change nothing for good.

focus.why: The action under the keyboard or the pointer becomes a small recess, so the position is shown by depth instead of a tint.

focus-visible.why: When the keyboard moved focus, the row also shows the same dark ring as every part, drawn inside the row.

aria-disabled=true.why: An action that cannot run now fades to half and does nothing when it is pressed, but stays in its place.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the panel keeps a real border and the focused row uses the system highlight for its edge.

data-side=top.why: When the panel flips above its key it rises from below instead, so it always grows out of the key (D-008).

data-state=open.why: Opening is a state change, so it moves. It rises in from @starting-style over motion.release on the decelerating curve (D-008).

data-state=closing.why: While it leaves, the part fades and sinks back over motion.exit on the accelerating curve, and no key or reader reaches it (D-008).

@media prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.why: Under Reduce motion nothing travels; only fades remain, on motion.hover, which the tokens keep (D-008).

transform.why: Opening is a state change, so it moves. The panel fades in from a rise toward the key (above or below, by data-side) over motion.release on the decelerating curve and leaves over motion.exit on the accelerating one (D-008). Under Reduce motion only the fade stays, on motion.hover.

opacity.why: Opening is a state change, so it moves. The panel fades in from a rise toward the key (above or below, by data-side) over motion.release on the decelerating curve and leaves over motion.exit on the accelerating one (D-008). Under Reduce motion only the fade stays, on motion.hover.

background-color.why: The reached row sinks into a well on motion.hover, fast on and slower off, so moving down the panel reads as a walk, never a jump.

box-shadow.why: The reached row sinks into a well on motion.hover, fast on and slower off, so moving down the panel reads as a walk, never a jump.
